description: The informal audit network among France, Germany, and Poland formalizes into a de facto parallel evaluation body, sharing real-time runtime telemetry and red-team findings across national agencies while bypassing the EU’s central oversight. This creates a two-tier governance system: Brussels’ authority erodes further as member states rely on this faster, more technically grounded channel for critical AI assurance.

A coalition of mid-sized EU member states, frustrated by Brussels' paralysis and dependency on external AI, begins informal coordination with Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan on shared access to secure compute and joint evaluation protocols. The network operates outside formal EU channels but leverages the Union's upstream semiconductor leverage to negotiate collective terms with providers. It signals a quiet realignment of middle powers seeking autonomy without confrontation.
